items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to establishing a next of kin registry for holders of drivers' licenses, learners' permits and non-driver identification cards
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S1910

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in
relation to establishing a next of kin registry for holders of
drivers' licenses, learners' permits and non-driver identification
cards

 PURPOSE :

To create a "next of kin registry" in the State of New York.

 SUMMARY :

Section 1 amends the Vehicle and Traffic Law  by adding a new section
(215-a) in order to require the commissioner of the Department of
Motor Vehicles to establish and operate a statewide internet
accessible website known as the "next of kin registry." The
commissioner of the Department of Motor Vehicles is required to create
a system by which the license/ID holder can sign in using their card
number and add emergency contacts who are 18 years or older. The
emergency contact will be contacted by an investigating police officer
in the event of an accident pursuant to the new Section 607 of the
Vehicle and Traffic Law provided for in Section 2 of this legislation.

Section 2 creates a new Section 607 of the Vehicle and Traffic Law in
order to provide notification of emergency contacts.

Section 3 provides the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

In the event of a motor vehicle accident, family members of the
victims should be informed in a timely manner. The current law
provides no way for police officers to find contact information for a
victims' emergency contacts in the event of an accident.

This bill establishes a statewide internet site to be known as the
"next of kin registry." Holders of drivers' licenses, learners'
permits and non-driver identification cards will be able to visit the
website and use their card number to register up to two emergency
contacts. The emergency contacts must be 18 years or older. In the
event of an accident resulting in physical injury, death, or
incapacitation, the investigating police officer will then attempt to
contact the emergency contact(s) provided for in the online registry.
Furthermore, this bill specifically provides protection for
registrants from disclosure under the Freedom of Information Law.
Only police officers in the specific instances outlined in this bill
will be permitted to access emergency contact information provided in
the "next of kin registry." This legislation will also allow New York
State's Department of Motor Vehicles to apply a similar system to
other states' online registries for "next of kin" emergency contacts.

Motor vehicle accidents are traumatic for victims and their family
members. In our technological age, it is inexcusable that anything
prevent the prompt notice of victims' next of kin in the event of an
accident resulting in physical injury, death, or incapacitation. This
legislation provides that notice in safe and efficient manner.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2011-2012: S.5276 Passed the Senate / A.8021 Referred to
Transportation
2013-2014: S.1948 Passed the Senate / A.9120 Referred to
Transportation
2015-2016: S.2396-A Passed the Senate/ A.6939-A

 FISCAL IMPACT :

Minimal.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the one hundred eightieth day after it
shall have become law; provided, that, effective immediately, any
actions necessary to implement the provisions of this act on its
effective date are authorized and directed to be completed on or
before such date.

summary: Directs the commissioner of motor vehicles to establish a next of kin registry for holders of drivers' licenses, learners' permits and non-driver identification cards; such holders may submit their emergency contact information to be used by police and medical services in the event the holder is injured or killed.
